vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: AWT, JavaFX). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u471, 8u471-b50, 8u471-perf, 11.0.29, 17.0.17, 21.0.9, 25.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.17 and 21.0.9; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.16. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the Liquibase Secure container. The image uses Temurin JRE and does not run as a sandboxed Java client.

ratings.justification: The assessed image is a Linux CLI container built on Temurin JRE, not an Oracle Java SE/GraalVM client runtime with AWT/JavaFX applet or Web Start exposure.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE AWT/JavaFX sandbox vulnerability. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1), not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client distribution. The container runs the Liquibase CLI through docker-entrypoint.sh rather than a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet environment (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so the client-only runtime required by the advisory is absent.

analysis.detail: JDK Security component (resource resolving) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse- temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse- temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java JSSE partial-denial-of-service issue. analysis.detail: Oracle Java 2D partial-denial-of-service issue. Both open PR #5075 and PR #5078 incorrectly treated this as already covered by merged PR #5071 (likely conflated with CVE-2026-47021, also a "2D" component JSSE-adjacent issue assessed there) -- it was not actually present in #5071 or on main, so this closes that gap. The scanned image reports Oracle OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-LTS; Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2). A source review found no java.awt or 2D API usage anywhere in the shipped runtime path, matching the code_not_reachable finding already recorded for CVE-2026-47021 and CVE-2026-47010 (same "2D"/ "ImageIO" component family). Oracle's own advisory note for this CVE goes further than the boilerplate applet note used elsewhere: it explicitly states the issue "does not apply to Java deployments, typically in servers, that load and run only trusted code (e.g., code installed by an administrator)" -- which is exactly Liquibase Secure's deployment model (a headless CLI running only its own installed code, not a sandboxed client executing untrusted 2D content).

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - April 2026

analysis.detail: This is a Java SE Security component issue (security-libs, java.security) from the April 2026 Critical Patch Update. It affects Java 21.0.10 and earlier and is fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.11. Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9, and 5.1.0 and 5.1.1 ship 21.0.10. 5.2.0 and later ship 21.0.11 or newer, so they already carry the fix. In the earlier images, exploitation is hard: the attacker must already have a logon to the host running the JVM and must deliver crafted data to the java.security APIs. That means a service that passes untrusted input to those APIs, or a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet client that runs untrusted code. Liquibase Secure is neither. It is a short-lived command-line client that starts no listener, runs no untrusted code, and only connects outbound to the database and service endpoints its operator configures. A successful attack yields at most limited read access.

Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u481, 8u481-b50, 8u481-perf, 11.0.30, 17.0.18, 21.0.10, 25.0.2, 26; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.18 and 21.0.10; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.17. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTPS to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure 5.2.0 and later, which ship a fixed JRE. Earlier releases are not exposed in their intended command-line use. Upgrading to 5.2.0 or later removes the reliance on that deployment condition.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure hosts no TLS service and runs no untrusted code in a Java sandbox; it only connects outbound to operator-configured endpoints, and 5.2.0 and later ship the fixed JRE.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - April 2026

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE JSSE partial-denial-of-service issue from the April 2026 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.11. The scan reported Temurin 21.0.10. The JRE in each published Liquibase Secure image is 21.0.8 in 5.0.0 and 5.0.1, 21.0.9 in 5.0.2 and 5.0.3, 21.0.10 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, and 21.0.11 or later from 5.2.0 onward, so 5.2.0 and later already carry the fix. For the earlier images, exploitation needs an attacker to send crafted HTTPS traffic to the affected JSSE code, for example by reaching a TLS service the JVM hosts, or a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet client that runs untrusted code. Liquibase Secure hosts no TLS service: it is a short-lived command-line client that starts no listener and only opens outbound TLS connections to the database and service endpoints its operator configures, so the only peer able to send it TLS data is one of those trusted endpoints or an attacker already in that network path.

vulnerabilities.description: An integer overflow in the tt_var_load_item_variation_store function of the Freetype library in versions 2.13.2 and 2.13.3 may allow for an out of bounds read operation when parsing HVAR/VVAR/MVAR tables in OpenType variable fonts. This issue is fixed in version 2.14.2.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure 5.2.0 and later, which ship a fixed JRE. Earlier releases never open a variable font: Liquibase loads no font files of its own and the image installs only static TrueType fonts.

ratings.justification: The overflow is reached only when the JDK's FreeType parses a variable font. Liquibase never loads a font file of its own and the image's only fonts are static TrueType fonts, and 5.2.0 and later ship the fixed JRE.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - April 2026

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE 2D (FreeType) issue from the April 2026 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.11. The flaw is an integer overflow in FreeType's tt_var_load_item_variation_store, reached only while FreeType parses the HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table of an OpenType variable font. The JDK ships its own FreeType (lib/libfreetype.so), which it uses to rasterise text: 2.13.3, in range, in the 21.0.8 to 21.0.10 JREs of Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.1.1, and the fixed 2.14.2 or later from 5.2.0. Exploitation needs the JVM to open an attacker-supplied variable font. The JDK opens either a font file passed to Font.createFont or a font that fontconfig lists from the system font directories, owned by root, or from per-user font directories that only the account running Liquibase can write. No class in the jars shipped in the 5.0.0 through 5.1.1 images calls Font.createFont. The image's only installed fonts are the DejaVu TrueType fonts under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu, which are static fonts with no fvar, HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table. The container entrypoint runs only the Liquibase CLI and the optional lpm helper, a statically linked Go binary.

Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u471, 8u471-b50, 8u471-perf, 11.0.29, 17.0.17, 21.0.9, 25.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.17 and 21.0.9; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.16. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later, which ship a fixed JRE. Earlier releases never use Java RMI. Upgrading to 5.1.0 or later removes the reliance on that condition.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure exports no RMI object and makes no RMI call, so the vulnerable component is never reached, and 5.1.0 and later ship the fixed JRE.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - January 2026

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE RMI component issue from the January 2026 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.10. The scan reported Temurin 21.0.8. The JRE in each published Liquibase Secure image is 21.0.8 in 5.0.0 and 5.0.1, 21.0.9 in 5.0.2 and 5.0.3, both in range, and 21.0.10 or later from 5.1.0 onward, so 5.1.0 and later already carry the fix. For the earlier images, exploitation needs the JVM to export or call RMI objects over the network. Liquibase Secure runs as a short-lived outbound command-line client: it exports no RMI object, starts no RMI registry and enables no remote JMX, and a source review found no use of the java.rmi or javax.management.remote APIs in Liquibase Secure. The container runs no sandboxed Java Web Start or applet runtime either, so no attacker-supplied data reaches the RMI component.

Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later, which ship a fixed JRE. Earlier releases are not exposed in their intended command-line use. Upgrading to 5.1.0 or later removes the reliance on that deployment condition.

ratings.justification: Exploitation needs user interaction with a sandboxed Java client or a service that feeds untrusted data to the Networking APIs. Neither matches the Liquibase Secure container deployment, and 5.1.0 and later ship the fixed JRE.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - January 2026

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE Networking component issue from the January 2026 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.10. The scan reported Temurin 21.0.8. The JRE in each published Liquibase Secure image is 21.0.8 in 5.0.0 and 5.0.1, 21.0.9 in 5.0.2 and 5.0.3, both in range, and 21.0.10 or later from 5.1.0 onward, so 5.1.0 and later already carry the fix. vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Install). ratings.justification: CNA (Oracle) score; NVD had not yet published its own score at assessment time.
The vulnerable component (Oracle's Java installer) is not present in the Liquibase Secure image; the container runs a Temurin JRE unpacked from a release archive.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE/GraalVM Install-component vulnerability, fixed upstream in 21.0.12 (Oracle August 2026 CPU). The flaw is in Oracle's Java installer, a packaging component that ships only with Oracle's own distribution. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) via docker-entrypoint.sh (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8); Temurin's JRE is unpacked from a release archive, not installed through Oracle's installer, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image at all. There is no Adoptium/Temurin tracking entry for this CVE. Unlike the other Oracle Java SE entries in this batch (sandbox/Web Start applicability mismatches, justified requires_environment), this is a component absence -- the installer isn't shipped at all -- hence code_not_present.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.8 (Confidentiality impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No immediate action required given the narrow, trusted-endpoint- compromise precondition. Track Eclipse Temurin's release of a 21-jre- noble image containing 21.0.12.1+1 and rebuild once available.

ratings.justification: Vulnerable JVM networking/TLS code is in Liquibase's execute path (outbound HTTPS/TLS JDBC client), but exploitation requires the attacker to already control or compromise a trusted peer -- not reachable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold there.

analysis.detail: JDK Networking (HTTP Connections) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse-temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.
